title: Conjugate measurement-induced evolution towards maximally mixed states in quadratic quantum systems
abstract: In an earlier work, we showed that, in the interaction-dominant setting, coupling the conjugate variables of a subsystem to distinct environment modes drives the subsystem to a maximally mixed state. Here, we extend the study to the full quadratic dynamics of a single-mode subsystem coupled to a two-mode environment, and identify the phase-space mechanism responsible for the asymptotic behavior. By tracking the exact reduced Weyl characteristic and Wigner functions, we demonstrate that they lose their dependence on local phase-space coordinates on every fixed compact region. In free-particle model, this happens for all values of coupling, whereas in the harmonic oscillator model, it happens above a critical value of the coupling. Under a finite-volume and momentum regularization, this behavior corresponds to the reduced subsystem approaching a maximally mixed state.
summary: This paper develops a rigorous theory showing how a quantum subsystem can approach a maximally mixed state purely through unitary evolution when coupled to an environment. It analyzes this phenomenon in quadratic systems, distinguishing between free-particle and harmonic oscillator dynamics. By using phase-space tools and regularization, the authors establish a clear phase-space mechanism for this non-equilibrium equilibration.
main_problem: The paper investigates the mechanism by which a reduced quantum subsystem approaches a maximally mixed state through strictly unitary dynamics, mimicking thermalization.
main_result: The reduced subsystem asymptotically approaches a maximally mixed state in both free-particle and harmonic oscillator models, with the mechanism depending on whether the dynamics induce phase-space shear or hyperbolic expansion.
method: The analysis uses phase-space representations, specifically tracking the reduced Wigner function and Weyl characteristic function, and employs finite-volume regularization to rigorously define the continuum limit.
model_or_system: The system is a quadratic quantum system partitioned into a subsystem (S) and an environment (E), modeled by a total quadratic Hamiltonian. The dynamics are governed by linear Heisenberg equations.
key_observables: Reduced Wigner function (WS), Weyl characteristic function ($\chi$), and the measure of local Wigner flattening ($\Delta_K(t)$).
important_parameters: Coupling constant ($g$), critical coupling value ($g_c$), and regularization parameters (finite volume $L$, momentum cutoff $N$).
main_assumptions: The analysis requires finite-volume and momentum regularization to make the maximally mixed state mathematically precise, and the underlying Hamiltonian is assumed to be quadratic.
paper_structure: The paper builds from general quadratic dynamics (Chunk 1) to detailed mathematical tools like Wigner/Weyl functions and environmental tracing (Chunk 2). It then analyzes the transition between dynamical regimes (e.g., critical coupling) and proves local Wigner flattening in the hyperbolic regime (Chunk 3). Finally, it situates the work within the broader literature of quantum relaxation (Chunk 4).
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous, purely unitary, and non-equilibrium mechanism for quantum thermalization in simple, exactly solvable models, which is highly relevant for understanding open quantum systems dynamics in quantum optics and AMO physics.
